problems.problem_statement: Find the gradient of the function \\(f(x, y) = x^2 y^3 + \\sin(\\pi x)\\) at the point \\((1, 2)\\).
problems.solution: The gradient of a function \\(f(x, y)\\) is given by the vector \\(\\\nabla f(x, y) = \\left< \\frac{\\\\partial f}{\\\\partial x}, \\frac{\\\\partial f}{\\\\partial y} \\right>\\). First, we compute the partial derivatives of \\(f(x, y) = x^2 y^3 + \\sin(\\pi x)\\):\\n\\n1. Partial derivative with respect to \\(x\\):\\n\\(\\\\frac{\\\\partial f}{\\\\partial x} = \\frac{\\\\partial}{\\\\partial x}(x^2 y^3 + \\sin(\\pi x)) = 2xy^3 + \\cos(\\pi x) \\\cdot \\pi = 2xy^3 + \\pi\\cos(\\pi x)\\) \\n\\n2. Partial derivative with respect to \\(y\\):\\n\\(\\\\frac{\\\\partial f}{\\\\partial y} = \\frac{\\\\partial}{\\\\partial y}(x^2 y^3 + \\sin(\\pi x)) = x^2(3y^2) = 3x^2y^2\\) \\n\\nNext, we evaluate these partial derivatives at the point \\((1, 2)\\):\\n\\n1. \\(\\\\frac{\\\\partial f}{\\\\partial x}(1, 2) = 2(1)(2)^3 + \\pi\\cos(\\pi \\cdot 1) = 2(8) + \\pi(-1) = 16 - \\pi\\)\\n\\n2. \\(\\\\frac{\\\\partial f}{\\\\partial y}(1, 2) = 3(1)^2(2)^2 = 3(1)(4) = 12\\)\\n\\nTherefore, the gradient vector at \\((1, 2)\\) is \\(\\\nabla f(1, 2) = \\left< 16 - \\pi, 12 \\right>\\).

scaffolding.hint: Recall that the gradient of a function \\(f(x, y)\\) is a vector of its partial derivatives: \\(\\\nabla f = \\left< \\frac{\\\\partial f}{\\\\partial x}, \\frac{\\\\partial f}{\\\\partial y} \\right>\\).
Compute the partial derivative of \\(f\\) with respect to \\(x\\). Remember to use the chain rule when differentiating the term \\(\\\\sin(\\pi x)\\).
Compute the partial derivative of \\(f\\) with respect to \\(y\\).
Substitute \\(x=1\\) and \\(y=2\\) into the expressions for the partial derivatives to find the components of the gradient vector at the specified point.
